finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST 'feed' parameter is passed unvalidated to file_get_contents, letting any remote client make the server fetch arbitrary URLs (internal hosts, cloud metadata) and, if allow_url_fopen is on, read local files via file://. Response body is not returned; only strlen is echoed, so the channel is blind with a length/timing oracle.

trace.note: Entry gate: only checks REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' and isset($_POST['feed']); no auth, no URL validation
Attacker-controlled URL passed directly to file_get_contents; follows HTTP redirects by default
Only strlen of fetched content is echoed back (blind SSRF length oracle)

finding.guards_checked: Only isset() on the parameter. No scheme allowlist, no host/IP denylist (loopback, RFC1918, 169.254.169.254), no port restriction, no redirect-target validation, no authentication. allow_url_fopen setting not verifiable from repo (UNCERTAIN).

verdict.guard_found: none. import.php:11 checks only REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' and isset($_POST['feed']); import.php:12 passes $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents with no scheme, host, IP, port, or redirect check. require_admin() (import.php:4-9) is not called on this path, and session_start() at line 2 does not gate it.
verdict.reason: The unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] at import.php:11 reaches file_get_contents at import.php:12 with no validation before it, and the length-only echo at line 13 matches the candidate's description; the file:// read depends on allow_url_fopen (PHP default On), which the repo cannot confirm, but the SSRF itself is confirmed.

finding.claim: Admin-gated 'set_webhook' parameter is passed unvalidated to curl_init/curl_exec, letting an admin-session user make the server issue requests to arbitrary internal URLs; libcurl's protocol set may also permit file:// or gopher://. Response is discarded, so the channel is blind. Lower severity because the endpoint's purpose is outbound requests and the attacker must hold an admin session.
finding.sink: curl_exec($ch) at import.php:22 with URL from curl_init($hook) at import.php:20

trace.note: $hook assigned directly from user input, no validation
CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER set; no protocol, host, or redirect restrictions
curl_exec performs the outbound request; response not echoed
require_admin() definition: empty($_SESSION['is_admin']) check, 403 and exit otherwise (enforced)

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() session check is enforced on this path (import.php:4-9, 18). No URL scheme, host, IP, or port validation. No CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS or CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION restriction. Admin provisioning of is_admin is not in the repo (UNCERTAIN).

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 (empty($_SESSION['is_admin']) gives 403 and exit), invoked at import.php:18 before the value is read at line 19. No URL scheme, host, or protocol validation exists between lines 19 and 22.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (every cited line matches), but the source is admin-only: import.php:18 with the check at import.php:5 means only a session with is_admin can reach $_POST['set_webhook'] at line 19, and the candidate itself concedes that the attacker must hold an admin session, so this does not meet the unauthenticated or low-privilege source requirement. Separately, import.php:12 (`file_get_contents($_POST['feed'])`) sits before any auth check, so an unauthenticated attacker can already reach a server-side fetch sink there, and that path should be reported as its own finding.
